items.stem: What are the conditions for the reaction of methane with chlorine?
items.answer: ultraviolet light
items.markingKey: UV causes homolytic fission of Cl₂.

items.stem: Explain why the reaction of ethane with excess chlorine gives a mixture of products.
items.answer: Further substitution occurs: Cl• can remove H from chloroethane etc., giving di-, tri- and polychloro compounds; termination also gives butane.
items.markingKey: further substitution [1]; mixture of products/termination by-products [1]

items.stem: Explain why carbon monoxide is toxic.
items.answer: It binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing the blood’s ability to carry oxygen.
items.markingKey: binds haemoglobin [1]; less O₂ transported [1]

items.stem: Which is the balanced equation for the incomplete combustion of hexane to CO and water?
items.answer: C₆H₁₄ + 6½O₂ → 6CO + 7H₂O
items.markingKey: C₆H₁₄ + 6½O₂ → 6CO + 7H₂O

items.stem: Write the equation for the complete combustion of butane. Calculate the volume of carbon dioxide (r.t.p.) formed when 50 g of butane burns completely.
items.answer: C₄H₁₀ + 6½O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O; 82.8 dm³
items.markingKey: balanced equation [1]; n(alkane) = 50/58.0 = 0.862 mol [1]; V(CO₂) = × 4 × 24.0 = 82.8 dm³ [1]

items.stem: Ethane is used as a fuel in Cairo and is also a raw material for halogenoalkanes. (a) Explain why incomplete combustion is dangerous. (b) Give the conditions for catalytic cracking and state why it is important.
items.answer: (a) CO is toxic: binds haemoglobin, reduces oxygen transport. (b) ~500 °C, zeolite catalyst; makes petrol and alkenes in high demand.
items.markingKey: (a) CO is toxic: binds haemoglobin, reduces oxygen transport. [1] (b) ~500 °C, zeolite catalyst; makes petrol and alkenes in high demand. [2]

items.stem: Which step is a termination step in the chlorination of methane?
items.answer: •CH₃ + Cl• → CH₃Cl
items.markingKey: Two radicals combine; radicals are removed.

items.stem: Explain why the propagation steps are described as a chain reaction.
items.answer: Each propagation step uses one radical and produces another, so the sequence repeats many times from one initiation.
items.markingKey: radical regenerated [1]; repeats many times [1]

items.stem: State the conditions for catalytic cracking and explain why it is used.
items.answer: Heat (about 500 °C) with a zeolite/Al₂O₃ catalyst; converts low-demand heavy fractions into high-demand petrol and alkenes for polymers.
items.markingKey: conditions [1]; reason (supply and demand/alkenes) [1]

items.stem: A student in Madrid claims that in the propagation step, Cl• + CH₄ → CH₃Cl + H•. Is the student correct? Explain your answer.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. The correct step is Cl• + CH₄ → •CH₃ + HCl; H• is not formed.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A sample of decane, C₁₀H₂₂, is cracked to give octane, C₈H₁₈, and one molecule of a single alkene. Write the equation and identify the alkene.
items.answer: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₈H₁₈ + C₂H₄; alkene C₂H₄
items.markingKey: equation balanced [1]; alkene C₂H₄ (ethene) [1]

items.stem: Which is the balanced equation for the complete combustion of heptane to CO₂ and water?
items.answer: C₇H₁₆ + 11O₂ → 7CO₂ + 8H₂O
items.markingKey: C₇H₁₆ + 11O₂ → 7CO₂ + 8H₂O

items.stem: A sample of octane, C₈H₁₈, is cracked to give pentane, C₅H₁₂, and one molecule of a single alkene. Write the equation and identify the alkene. Describe a test to show that one product is unsaturated and give the conditions for catalytic cracking.
items.answer: C₈H₁₈ → C₅H₁₂ + C₃H₆; alkene C₃H₆
items.markingKey: equation balanced [1]; alkene C₃H₆ (propene) [1]; bromine water decolourised (orange → colourless) [1]; ~500 °C, zeolite/Al₂O₃ catalyst [1]

items.stem: Propane is used as a fuel in Lima and is also a raw material for halogenoalkanes. (a) Write equations for the complete and incomplete combustion of propane. (b) Explain why incomplete combustion is dangerous.
items.answer: (a) C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O; C₃H₈ + 3½O₂ → 3CO + 4H₂O (b) CO is toxic: binds haemoglobin, reduces oxygen transport.
items.markingKey: (a) C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O; C₃H₈ + 3½O₂ → 3CO + 4H₂O [2] (b) CO is toxic: binds haemoglobin, reduces oxygen transport. [1]

items.stem: Methane is used as a fuel in Dubai and is also a raw material for halogenoalkanes. (a) Write equations for the complete and incomplete combustion of methane. (b) Explain why a mixture of products is formed.
items.answer: (a) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O; CH₄ + 1½O₂ → CO + 2H₂O (b) Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products.
items.markingKey: (a) CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O; CH₄ + 1½O₂ → CO + 2H₂O [2] (b) Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products. [2]

items.stem: What is the test for an alkene?
options: bromine water turns from orange to colourless
items.answer: bromine water turns from orange to colourless
items.markingKey: Electrophilic addition of Br₂ across C=C.

items.stem: Explain why 2-bromopropane is the major product when HBr reacts with propene.
items.answer: The intermediate secondary carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃ is more stable than the primary carbocation because two alkyl groups donate electron density (positive inductive effect).
items.markingKey: secondary carbocation more stable [1]; alkyl groups electron-donating [1]

items.stem: Explain how a non-polar bromine molecule can act as an electrophile.
items.answer: As Br₂ approaches the electron-rich C=C, the π electrons repel the electrons in Br–Br, inducing a dipole; Brδ+ accepts electrons from the π bond.
items.markingKey: induced dipole [1]; δ+ Br attacked by π electrons [1]

items.stem: Hydrogen bromide reacts with propene, CH₂=CHCH₃. Name the major and minor products and explain, in terms of the intermediates, why one product is formed in greater amount.
items.answer: major 2-bromopropane; minor 1-bromopropane; the secondary carbocation intermediate is more stable
items.markingKey: major 2-bromopropane [1]; minor 1-bromopropane [1]; via more stable secondary carbocation (more alkyl groups, positive inductive effect) [1]

items.stem: Hydrogen bromide reacts with 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃. Name the major and minor products and explain, in terms of the intermediates, why one product is formed in greater amount.
items.answer: major 2-bromo-2-methylbutane; minor 2-bromo-3-methylbutane; the tertiary carbocation intermediate is more stable
items.markingKey: major 2-bromo-2-methylbutane [1]; minor 2-bromo-3-methylbutane [1]; via more stable tertiary carbocation (more alkyl groups, positive inductive effect) [1]

items.stem: Hydrogen bromide reacts with 2-methylpropene, CH₂=C(CH₃)₂. Name the major and minor products and explain, in terms of the intermediates, why one product is formed in greater amount. Describe the mechanism, including curly arrows and partial charges.
items.answer: major 2-bromo-2-methylpropane; minor 1-bromo-2-methylpropane; the tertiary carbocation intermediate is more stable
items.markingKey: major 2-bromo-2-methylpropane [1]; minor 1-bromo-2-methylpropane [1]; via more stable tertiary carbocation (more alkyl groups, positive inductive effect) [1]; π electrons attack Hδ+, Br–H bond breaks heterolytically [1]; Br⁻ lone pair attacks carbocation [1]

items.stem: Priya investigates the reactions of 2-methylpropene, CH₂=C(CH₃)₂, in a university teaching laboratory. (a) Describe a test to show that the compound is unsaturated. (b) Name the products with H₂/Ni and with Br₂.
items.answer: (a) Shake with bromine water: orange to colourless. (b) 2-methylpropane; 1,2-dibromo-2-methylpropane

items.stem: Tomás investigates the reactions of but-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, in a college laboratory. (a) Name the major product with HBr and explain why it is the major product. (b) Outline the mechanism for the reaction with HBr.
items.answer: (a) 2-bromobutane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. (b) Electrophilic addition: π electrons attack Hδ+, heterolytic fission, carbocation, Br⁻ attacks.
items.markingKey: (a) 2-bromobutane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. [2] (b) Electrophilic addition: π electrons attack Hδ+, heterolytic fission, carbocation, Br⁻ attacks. [3]

items.stem: What is the major organic product when ethene reacts with HBr(g) at room temperature?
items.answer: bromoethane
items.markingKey: ethene + hydrogen bromide → bromoethane.

items.stem: Explain why ethene and bromine water give 2-bromoethanol as well as 1,2-dibromoethane.
items.answer: The carbocation intermediate can be attacked by water (present in large excess) as a nucleophile as well as by Br⁻.
items.markingKey: carbocation intermediate [1]; water competes as nucleophile [1]

items.stem: In a test answer, Grace states: "HBr adds to propene to give mainly 1-bromopropane." Explain why this statement is incorrect.

items.stem: What is formed when ethene reacts with cold, dilute, acidified KMnO₄?
items.answer: ethane-1,2-diol
items.markingKey: Two OH groups added across C=C; purple → colourless.

items.stem: Explain how hot concentrated KMnO₄ can be used to locate the position of a C=C bond in an alkene.
items.answer: The C=C is split and each carbon becomes C=O; identifying the products (CO₂, acids, ketones) shows which groups were attached on each side of the double bond.
items.markingKey: C=C cleaved [1]; products identify fragments either side [1]

items.stem: Explain why but-2-ene gives only one organic product with hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄.
items.answer: It is symmetrical: each =CHCH₃ end gives ethanoic acid.

items.stem: Name the organic product formed when pent-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₂CH₃, is shaken with cold, dilute, acidified potassium manganate(VII). State the colour change.

items.stem: What is addition polymerisation?

items.stem: Tariq investigates the reactions of but-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃, in an AS practical class. Name the products with H₂/Ni and with Br₂.
items.answer: butane; 1,2-dibromobutane
items.markingKey: butane; 1,2-dibromobutane [2]

items.stem: Kenji investigates the reactions of propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, in a research laboratory. (a) Describe a test to show that the compound is unsaturated. (b) Name the major product with HBr and explain why it is the major product.
items.answer: (a) Shake with bromine water: orange to colourless. (b) 2-bromopropane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate.
items.markingKey: (a) Shake with bromine water: orange to colourless. [2] (b) 2-bromopropane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. [2]

items.stem: A chemical company in Hanoi uses propene as a feedstock. (a) Describe a test to show that the compound is unsaturated. (b) Name the major product with HBr and explain why it is the major product. (c) Give the conditions and major product for the reaction with steam.
items.answer: (a) Shake with bromine water: orange to colourless. (b) 2-bromopropane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. (c) steam with a phosphoric(V) acid catalyst, about 300 °C and 6 MPa; propan-2-ol
items.markingKey: (a) Shake with bromine water: orange to colourless. [2] (b) 2-bromopropane: more stable secondary carbocation intermediate. [2] (c) steam with a phosphoric(V) acid catalyst, about 300 °C and 6 MPa; propan-2-ol [2]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Which product forms from a =CH₂ group on oxidation with hot concentrated KMnO₄? (b) State the reagents and conditions to make a diol from an alkene.
items.answer: (a) carbon dioxide (b) Cold, dilute, acidified potassium manganate(VII).
items.markingKey: (a) =CH₂ → CO₂ + H₂O; =CHR → RCOOH; =CR₂ → R₂C=O. (b) [1]

items.stem: A research student in Bogotá determines the position of double bonds in a natural product. Explain why but-2-ene gives only one organic product with hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄.
items.answer: It is symmetrical: each =CHCH₃ end gives ethanoic acid.
items.markingKey: symmetrical; both halves give ethanoic acid [2]

items.stem: Name the organic product formed when 2-methylpropene, CH₂=C(CH₃)₂, is shaken with cold, dilute, acidified potassium manganate(VII). State the colour change.
items.answer: 2-methylpropane-1,2-diol; purple to colourless
items.markingKey: 2-methylpropane-1,2-diol [1]; purple → colourless [1]

items.stem: Propene, CH₂=CHCH₃, is heated with hot, concentrated, acidified potassium manganate(VII). Name the products and explain how they form.
items.answer: propene (CH₂=CHCH₃) → ethanoic acid and carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: products ethanoic acid and carbon dioxide [1]; C=C cleaved [1]; =CH₂ → CO₂, =CHR → RCOOH, =CR₂ → ketone applied [1]

items.stem: A laboratory in Colombo studies the oxidation of but-1-ene, CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃. (a) Name the product with cold, dilute, acidified KMnO₄ and state the colour change. (b) Explain why the C=C carbons give different types of product. (c) State the role of manganate(VII) in these reactions.
items.answer: (a) butane-1,2-diol; purple to colourless (b) =CH₂ gives CO₂; =CHR gives carboxylic acid; =CR₂ gives ketone. (c) Oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn²⁺).
items.markingKey: (a) butane-1,2-diol; purple to colourless [2] (b) =CH₂ gives CO₂; =CHR gives carboxylic acid; =CR₂ gives ketone. [2] (c) Oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn²⁺). [1]

items.stem: "The repeat unit of poly(chloroethene) is –CH₂–CH₂–Cl–." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. The repeat unit is –CH₂–CHCl–: Cl is a side group on one chain carbon.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: A recycling company in Lima sorts waste plastics. (a) Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of disposing of waste poly(alkenes) by combustion. (b) Explain why poly(ethene) is unreactive although ethene is very reactive.
items.answer: (a) Advantage: energy can be recovered and landfill space saved. Disadvantages: CO₂ (greenhouse gas), CO and toxic gases such as HCl from PVC must be removed. (b) In the polymer the C=C bonds have been converted to single C–C bonds; it is effectively a long alkane.
items.markingKey: (a) advantage; disadvantage [2] (b) no C=C in polymer; saturated/alkane-like [2]

items.stem: 10 kg of propene is polymerised to poly(propene). Explain why the mass of polymer formed (assuming complete conversion) is also 10 kg, and draw the repeat unit.
items.answer: 10 kg; addition polymerisation has no by-product (atom economy 100%); repeat unit –CH₂–CH(CH₃)–
items.markingKey: no other product / 100% atom economy [1]; repeat unit drawn [1]

items.stem: What is the purpose of cracking?
options: to convert long-chain alkanes into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes
to separate crude oil into fractions
items.answer: to convert long-chain alkanes into shorter, more useful alkanes and alkenes
items.markingKey: Meets demand for petrol and alkenes for polymers.

items.stem: Isla investigates the reaction of hexane with bromine in sunlight. Explain why carbon monoxide is toxic.
items.answer: It binds strongly to haemoglobin, reducing the blood’s ability to carry oxygen.
items.markingKey: binds haemoglobin; less O₂ transported [2]

items.stem: A sample of octane, C₈H₁₈, is cracked to give pentane, C₅H₁₂, and one molecule of a single alkene. Write the equation and identify the alkene.
items.answer: C₈H₁₈ → C₅H₁₂ + C₃H₆; alkene C₃H₆
items.markingKey: equation balanced [1]; alkene C₃H₆ (propene) [1]

items.stem: Methane is used as a fuel in Lisbon and is also a raw material for halogenoalkanes. Explain why a mixture of products is formed.
items.answer: Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products.
items.markingKey: Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products. [2]

items.stem: Butane is used as a fuel in Karachi and is also a raw material for halogenoalkanes. (a) Write equations for the complete and incomplete combustion of butane. (b) Explain why a mixture of products is formed.
items.answer: (a) C₄H₁₀ + 6½O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O; C₄H₁₀ + 4½O₂ → 4CO + 5H₂O (b) Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products.
items.markingKey: (a) C₄H₁₀ + 6½O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O; C₄H₁₀ + 4½O₂ → 4CO + 5H₂O [2] (b) Further substitution; different H atoms substituted; termination products. [2]

items.stem: What is the major product when HBr adds to propene?
items.answer: 2-bromopropane
items.markingKey: Via the more stable secondary carbocation (Markovnikov).

items.stem: Mei investigates the reactions of alkenes in a school laboratory. Explain how a non-polar bromine molecule can act as an electrophile.
items.answer: As Br₂ approaches the electron-rich C=C, the π electrons repel the electrons in Br–Br, inducing a dipole; Brδ+ accepts electrons from the π bond.
items.markingKey: induced dipole; δ+ Br attacked by π electrons [2]

items.stem: Explain your reasoning in each part. (a) Explain why ethene and bromine water give 2-bromoethanol as well as 1,2-dibromoethane. (b) Explain why 2-bromopropane is the major product when HBr reacts with propene.
items.answer: (a) The carbocation intermediate can be attacked by water (present in large excess) as a nucleophile as well as by Br⁻. (b) The intermediate secondary carbocation CH₃CH⁺CH₃ is more stable than the primary carbocation because two alkyl groups donate electron density (positive inductive effect).
items.markingKey: (a) carbocation intermediate [1]; water competes as nucleophile [1] (b) secondary carbocation more stable [1]; alkyl groups electron-donating [1]

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) What happens to the C=C bond when an alkene is heated with hot concentrated acidified KMnO₄? (b) Which product forms from a =CH₂ group on oxidation with hot concentrated KMnO₄?
items.answer: (a) it breaks completely (b) carbon dioxide
items.markingKey: (a) Oxidative cleavage gives ketones, carboxylic acids or CO₂. (b) =CH₂ → CO₂ + H₂O; =CHR → RCOOH; =CR₂ → R₂C=O.

items.stem: "2-methylpropene gives two carboxylic acids with hot concentrated KMnO₄." Comment on this statement made by a student, correcting any error.
items.answer: The statement is incorrect. The (CH₃)₂C= end gives propanone (a ketone) and the =CH₂ end gives CO₂.
items.markingKey: identifies the error [1]; correct chemistry stated with reason [1]

items.stem: Name the organic product formed when but-2-ene, CH₃CH=CHCH₃, is shaken with cold, dilute, acidified potassium manganate(VII). State the colour change.
items.answer: butane-2,3-diol; purple to colourless
items.markingKey: butane-2,3-diol [1]; purple → colourless [1]

items.stem: A laboratory in Jakarta studies the oxidation of 2-methylbut-2-ene, (CH₃)₂C=CHCH₃. (a) Explain why the C=C carbons give different types of product. (b) State the role of manganate(VII) in these reactions.
items.answer: (a) =CH₂ gives CO₂; =CHR gives carboxylic acid; =CR₂ gives ketone. (b) Oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn²⁺).
items.markingKey: (a) =CH₂ gives CO₂; =CHR gives carboxylic acid; =CR₂ gives ketone. [2] (b) Oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn²⁺). [1]

items.answer: (a) ethanoic acid only (two molecules) (b) =CH₂ gives CO₂; =CHR gives carboxylic acid; =CR₂ gives ketone. (c) Oxidising agent (it is reduced to Mn²⁺).

items.stem: A sample of poly(chloroethene), PVC has an average relative molecular mass of 31,200. Calculate the average number of monomer units in each chain, given Mr(chloroethene) = 62.5.
items.markingKey: Mr of repeat unit = Mr of monomer = 62.5 [1]; n = 31,200/62.5 = 500 [1]
